speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs (a) how will Singapore support the 20-point peace plan for Gaza proposed by the United States; and (b) whether Singapore will consider playing a role in the peace plan if it is accepted by both Israel and Hamas.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs (a) how does the Government assess the viability of the Gaza peace plan in advancing a two-state solution; and (b) what role can Singapore play to contribute constructively, including the possible recognition of a Palestinian state under suitable conditions.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I believe Mr Gerald Giam1 has also filed a question, similar topic, for a subsequent Sitting.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I will try to address the issue in this reply and also be happy to take supplementary questions.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And if that is adequate, the Member can withdraw his Parliamentary Question that was filed for a later session.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I need to commend the incredible achievement of President Trump, his negotiating team, which includes Mr Steve Witkoff, Marco Rubio, Jared Kushner and also, the invaluable part played by Egypt, Qatar and Turkey.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is a critical plan and it is not just the details of the plan or how many points there are.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And this is crucial, this is important, this is the first step of what will, in fact, be a long and arduous journey to peace.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I would also expect and hope that there will be some United Nations (UN) Security Council resolution to provide an international legal framework for these arrangements.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, now let me turn to what we are doing and are hoping to do more of on the humanitarian front.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In the past two years, we have been working very closely with the Egyptian Red Crescent, with the Jordanian Hashemite Charity Organisation.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We are also working with the World Food Programme; and we are also working with a few Egyptian hospitals, in fact, the medical team from the National University Hospital was just there a few weeks ago.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We have also deployed as and when there has been hospital ships in the area to provide medical treatment to people who need help.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I think the immediate acceleration of humanitarian assistance now, is the fact that I hope the over land routes will open.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: That is crucial if humanitarian assistance is going to be delivered at the scale necessary.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, we will certainly look forward to doing more with our partners in the region and I would add, we also expect the Israelis to do their part to facilitate the delivery of humanitarian assistance over land through the crossings into Gaza.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We have already been working with them for years – capacity-building programmes, technical assistance, more recently, scholarships.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And all this with a view to enhancing the capacity, to exercise effective administrative oversight and to exercise the levers of government in their eventual statehood.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I would expect to increase the tempo of our interaction with the Palestinian Authority so that they can fulfil this ambition.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Again, we will need time and we will stand ready to respond to the Palestinian Authority's assessment of its own needs and particularly, I hope its ability to exercise governance in Gaza as well, an area in which it has not been able to exercise governance for two decades.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I just want to give this House the assurance that we are watching developments very closely and we will do our best within the limits and constraints of distance and the fact that we are very small, but we happen to have a multiracial, multi-religious united society who is open-hearted, generous and willing to do, in a sense, more than our fair share to help people in need in this very dire set of circumstances.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: And thank you to the Minister for the comprehensive reply.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: When I submitted this Parliamentary Question, the 20-point peace plan was yet to be accepted by Hamas and Israel.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: We are glad that the plan has now been accepted and the hostages have been released.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: And two, will the Minister also consider setting up a school, for example, in Gaza, to educate the young that have very little opportunity to access quality education?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: And thirdly, will Singapore consider sending a small peacekeeping team to provide logistic support to the bigger efforts led by the US?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Of course, I am suggesting this when the situation is more stable.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We look forward to doing more with our partners.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But it depends very much on access, on security and on the needs.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I would make this point from a medical perspective.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: At this stage, you are not dealing with the immediate acute trauma.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In fact, you are dealing with difficult sequelae like amputations, the need for prosthesis, the need for rehabilitation, the need to deal with psychological and emotional trauma.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, it is a different set of of specialties that are necessary.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And my point again is depending on the needs and depending on our resources, we will do our part.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The exact locations of deployment are again dictated by exigencies on the ground.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Where are the facilities in which our medical staff can make a contribution?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And to that end, I am sure this House will agree, we also want to pay attention to the safety of our staff on the ground.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: On schools, well, I think we should be cognisant that there are very few Arab fluent speakers in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But to the extent that we can work with "train the trainer" programmes, and in the long run, there is going to be a need for education, and vocational education and training, which will help enhance their ability to acquire the skills which are necessary for the long-term economy.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I hope there will be one and we will assess very carefully what role we can contribute.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It would be premature for me to make any commitments at this stage.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I had a supplementary question on humanitarian aid assistance and I am heartened to hear that Singapore will continue to work with the international bodies, and at the same time maintain the safety of our humanitarian workers there.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: My question is on the President Trump brokered peace deal.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: While it covers the phased withdrawal and also ceasefire, it leaves the questions of Palestinian statehood and the governance in Gaza unresolved.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Does the Government view this as a credible step towards a genuine two-state solution?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And then, as a follow-up question to that, I agree with the Minister that it may be too early or premature to tell whether this peace plan would be enduring and effective.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But if it does lead to peace and stability for both the Israelis and the Palestinian people, we have to give credit where credit is due.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Would Singapore nominate or support President Trump for the Nobel Peace Prize?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is a first and essential step – but not sufficient to achieving peace, security, development, hope and even ultimately a two-state solution.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I think I just delivered a Ministerial Statement and we spent two or more than two hours on this subject a month ago.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I think this agreement sets the stage where it is possible to imagine a negotiated two-state solution can emerge.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I also want to remind everyone this has been one of the most intractable conflicts, not just of the last century, but going back a very long time.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And whilst we are all cheered by the current positive news, I think we should be very realistic and psychologically be prepared that this will be a long and arduous journey.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: For Singapore, we should maintain our consistent principled approach.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We should continue to have effective bridges and access to all the stakeholders.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We should, wherever possible, within the limits of our capability, be constructive, reliable partners for peace for development and long-term reconciliation between two peoples who have been through unimaginable horrors in the last two years.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This board includes former British Prime Minister Tony Blair.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The Minister has said that things are still inchoate, but would he agree that if we wait until it is fully formed, we would have missed the opportunity to get a seat on the board.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This is where we have a clear comparative advantage.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: It is a unique opportunity to contribute expertise and experience in nation building, and we could help build peace in the Middle East, and I dare say, even the wider world, given the global nature of this conflict.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Has the Ministry considered going beyond the regular Singapore Cooperation Programme, which typically invites selects Palestinian civil servants to attend training in Singapore, and instead send our senior civil servants or retired civil civil servants there to set up the administrative frameworks and structures and train the civil servants over there?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But let me take a step back and remind everybody.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I would also remind you that it is not just under the Singapore Cooperation Programme by which we engage the Palestinian Authority.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We have been having regular meetings at senior levels.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We will customise specific programmes that are relevant for them, but they will take the lead on which programmes they're interested in and how Singapore can best address their needs.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I hope Members of the House will agree with me that this understated, more discrete, behind-the-scenes, helpful, respectful approach is more appropriate for us in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I just want to talk a bit about humanitarian aid.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The Minister mentioned that multiple countries and non-governmental organisations are already providing aid and providing relief.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: So, how does Singapore ensure our aid compliments rather than duplicates international efforts?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And have we identified specific gaps in the international response where Singapore's niche support can add the most value?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And lastly, can the Minister explain why sustaining our humanitarian and diplomatic engagement in Gaza matters to Singaporeans, not as an act of compassion, but as a reflection of our identity as a small nation committed to peace and multiracial harmony?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There are many in international aid agencies involved and I would highlight first the UN itself, the UN's Work and Relief Committee, which has been doing work there for decades, in fact.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is not for us to impose our idea of how aid should be delivered.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, again, I hope Members understand my position of not trying to be pushy, and not trying to aim for positions on boards, and not trying to excessively draw attention, but just to quietly and effectively work in the background.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The other supplementary question is why do we do this?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And we do this because first it is an expression of Singaporeans' innate generosity and compassion.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Second, I believe in fact, that Singapore does have some significant resonance in the Middle East.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I have shared with this House before that when a Singapore delegation goes there, the diversity of the delegation – multi-religious, multiracial – has special resonance there.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Because there you have an example of conflicts over land, but turbo-charged by appeals to religious and other tribal instincts.

The example that a Singapore, united, cohesive, in the midst of our great diversity, and able to stand on our own two feet and then, to generously help enhance other people's capacity to also stand on their own two feet, is something which I believe, does also reflect well on our society.
I think it reflects the basic decency, goodwill and generosity that exists in the hearts of all Singaporeans.
But having said that, I would also add: there are many other trouble spots in the world.

And right now, if you look at what is happening in Sudan, or even if you look at the sequela of what has happened in Syria, in Yemen, there are many other trouble spots, on which in due time, I think people will also hope that Singaporeans respond to accordingly.
